narrative:
The 2020 Arizona Diamondbacks entered baseball's pandemic-shortened 60-game season with genuine optimism, boasting a capable rotation headlined by offseason acquisition Madison Bumgarner and an offense anchored by Ketel Marte and Starling Marte. But from the very first weekend, the warning signs were there. Bumgarner's debut was upstaged by the opposition, the bullpen leaked runs at critical moments, and a team that looked built to compete found itself treading water through a brutal July schedule.

August offered a brief reprieve. The Diamondbacks strung together an 11-16 month that, while below .500, represented their best sustained stretch of the year. There were moments of genuine life — Starling Marte coming through in clutch spots, Eduardo Escobar providing pop — but the bullpen remained a recurring liability, surrendering leads at the worst possible times. The high-leverage moments skewed dark, as Arizona's relievers repeatedly found themselves in the middle of damaging rallies they could not extinguish.

September brought the final reckoning. Mookie Betts and the Dodgers tormented Arizona's pitching staff, a Junior Guerra error turned a sacrifice bunt into a nightmare, and the month devolved into a 11-14 slog that buried any remaining playoff hopes. The Diamondbacks finished 25-35, the worst record in the NL West, a painful outcome for a franchise that had reached the NLDS just three years prior.

The 2020 season will be remembered as a lost campaign defined by bullpen collapses and an offense that could not manufacture enough runs to overcome its pitching deficiencies. With only 269 runs scored against 295 allowed in a shortened season, the math was simply never in Arizona's favor. The silver linings were few — flashes from Starling Marte, Escobar's occasional thunder — but they were not enough to alter a narrative that was written in those painful first weeks of July.

chapters.title: Rough Opening Act
chapters.description: Arizona stumbles out of the gate in July, with Bumgarner's debut going sideways and the bullpen surrendering critical leads.

chapters.title: Late-July Fight
chapters.description: The Diamondbacks show some resilience with clutch hits from Starling Marte and Escobar, but costly bullpen meltdowns erase the gains.

chapters.title: August Survival
chapters.description: Arizona posts its best month at 11-16, grinding out wins even as the high-leverage moments continue to cut against them.

chapters.title: Eduardo's Painful Night
chapters.description: A three-run Escobar home run in a losing effort on August 16th signals the end of August's modest optimism.

chapters.title: September Collapse
chapters.description: The Dodgers and others hammer Arizona's depleted pitching staff in September, ending any lingering playoff dreams.
